A.biggest_strength: Interactive customization that lets users test arbitrary 32-bit ISNs, generate random ISNs, adjust payload lengths, and toggle Wireshark-style relative sequence numbering.
A.biggest_weakness: Poor mobile responsiveness where the ladder diagram enforces a 480px minimum width, completely cutting off the server lifeline and state badges on 390px screens.

B.biggest_strength: A tangible visual byte-stream representation featuring individual sequence slots and animated SND.NXT and RCV.NXT pointers, which visually demonstrates why SYN and FIN consume sequence numbers.
B.biggest_weakness: Sequence numbers and payload data are hardcoded to fixed values (1000, 5000, 5-byte 'hello') with no input controls to test arbitrary ISNs or payloads.

structured_output.reasons: Page B is the overall winner because it visually demonstrates the actual mechanism of TCP sequence and acknowledgment tracking rather than just calculating numbers in a text panel. Its dual-strip byte-stream visualization with sliding SND.NXT and RCV.NXT pointers and color-coded formula makes the core concept of sequence space consumption immediately intuitive for networking students. In addition, Page B reflows seamlessly onto mobile viewports without horizontal clipping, whereas Page A completely cuts off the server side of the connection on phone screens.
